commits.message:
Markdown reads Python's whitespace in headings, code spans and HTML blocks, as markdown-it-py does (rich-unfiled-791c.gk3c)

Review fixes: an ATX heading opens at the end of the line as at a space or
tab, and its text may hold U+2028/U+2029; a paragraph keeps the indentation
past its container's margin, so a code span crossing a line ending keeps it,
the inline line-ending and escape rules dropping it everywhere else; HTML
tag patterns read Python's \s. Python's str.strip has one home,
src/renderables/python-space.ts, shared with markdown-url.ts.

Markdown reads only spaces and tabs as block whitespace, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.gk3c)

A no-break space at a line's edge was dropped and a line of them read as
blank, because the block pass trimmed with JavaScript's trim. markdown-it
reads only space and tab there (isStrSpace): isBlank is now a line with
nothing past its LEAD, a continuation line loses only that, and a heading
needs a space or tab after its #s. What markdown-it-py strips a paragraph,
a heading and a table cell of is Python's str.strip, not trim — U+FEFF
kept, U+0085 and U+001C–U+001F taken — so strip() over PYTHON_SPACE is
that one definition, and a table's body ends at a row it empties. Indented
code ends at its last non-blank line rather than popping trimmed strings.
Every case is pinned to Rich 15's output.

Markdown reads a link's destination and title as markdown-it does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz) (#434)

* Markdown reads a link's destination and title as markdown-it does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz)

linkDestination scanned a bare destination to the end of the text for every
`](` whose brackets matched, with no nesting cap, so `[*a](` repeated 20000
times took 14 s. destinationAt is now markdown-it's parseLinkDestination: at
most 32 parentheses open and all of them closed, ended only by an ASCII space
or control character or a backslash-space, and an angled destination that
honours escapes and is no destination without its `>`. LINK_TAIL is the link
rule's tail: a title only after a space, backslash escapes in it, markdown-it's
space rather than Unicode's. Every case is pinned to Rich 15's output.

* Markdown reads a link's tail in linear time and a lone CR as a line ending, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz)

Review (high) fixes: the space after a destination is skipped once, as
markdown-it's link rule does, instead of split two ways by one regex — 100k
spaces took six seconds; one LINK_SPACE pattern is now the only definition
of link space; parseMarkdown ends a line at \r as markdown-it normalizes it.
